newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev falls to 207.50-211 per dlr at close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev falls to 207.50-211 per dlr at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed in a wide spread between 207.50 and 211 per dollar, weaker than 204.50-205 at the opening due a sharp rise in foreign currency demand on the domestic interbank market, dealers said.

"Trade was hectic and in large volumes as a big fuel importer was bidding for dollars and the lev hit a fresh low of 211 at noon. But the market calmed down in the afternoon," a commercial bank dealer said.
According to other traders the client was searching for some $2 million and that demand was probably met by midday because almost no deals were struck in the afternoon.
The central bank has probably sold a limited dollar volume to the importer in a bid to take some pressure off the weakening lev, dealers said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
The longer period to value date of today's spot deals also contributed to the lev's slide, dealers said.
Their value date falls on Tuesday, September 3, because U.S. markets will be closed on Monday for Labour Day.
The lev closed at 202.90-203.30 per dollar on Wednesday.
